paragraphs.source_en: The Ashikaga shogunate had fallen, and there could no longer be any doubt that Takeda Shingen—the man who had caused Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu such endless trouble—was dead. Shingen's son Katsuyori commanded the retainers left behind and fancied himself powerful, but Ieyasu had already begun to hold them in check. The next task was to suppress the forces of Honganji and the uprisings of the Ikkō adherents who supported it. It was a matter of repaying violence in kind.
